title: Restore durable lead conversions through the real ledger and consented Google mirror

source.ref: Daniel requested completing all analytics work and removing repeated handoff approval checkpoints; live data inspection exposed an unregistered durable-lead event.

detail: The actual durable lead helper emitted lead.captured, but the closed taxonomy dropped it before the engagement ledger and no generate_lead mapping existed. This registers the event as server-authoritative and restores the existing tracking chain. A nonempty stable durable-lead key and successful first insert are mandatory; duplicates and ledger failures cannot mirror. The lead-only Google branch requires a real validated numeric browser client/session identity, a closed five-value source catalog, fresh canonical browser consent, verified request account consent and actual platform/team staff exclusion. Only the explicit AuthSessionMissingError is treated as an anonymous session; unavailable auth/profile/team evidence fails closed. The own-profile read is bound to the server-verified auth user, and real database staff roles remain authoritative under view-as. A minimal dynamically loaded server leaf performs one bounded service-role team-membership read, transparently recorded as one new admin-client baseline entry under Daniel’s instruction to bypass handoff approval loops and root’s explicit security review. No generic analytics policy is broadened. The Google payload uses only lead_source from the closed catalog and the browser identity, never contact details, durable IDs, private support/reflection fields or fabricated identity. Existing lead helper call contracts and tests remain byte-identical. The new actual-chain probe exercises real helper, registry, track, engagement recorder and GA transport with request/database/network boundaries isolated: untouched main fails23 and passes4 assertions; the candidate passes all27. This implementation does not claim historical conversion backfill or production deployment. No SQL, provider configuration, real Google events or email sends are performed by this change. Final focused verification passes97 tests across10 files, including existing lead caller contracts, real Google payload tests, canonical cookie-consent cases, and new actual /api/track rejection tests proving browser-spoofed lead events are rejected before auth, ledger or Google transport. Six changed JavaScript/TypeScript files pass ESLint; the admin-client guard passes895 importers against895 baseline entries. Root reviewed the privacy design and an independent GA4 reviewer passed39 tests across three files and found no blocking issue. The actual client reachability audit confirms journey-settings imports its pure meeting helper and practices is server-only; the old track comment no longer describes that path. New request policy loads only on the lead branch and avoids the heavy auth.ts import graph; a real preview remains required before deployment. Before publication, root and the separate consent-restoration owner approved naming the new leaf server-google-policy.ts/requestGoogleAllowed for reuse by other request-backed mirrors. This is a filename/export rename only; the27 frozen actual-chain assertions and the probe bytes retain their original SHA256 values. Repeated final focused verification after the rename remains97 tests/10 files and six-file lint passing; admin-client counts remain895/895. The previous full required backlog run passed2695 entries/1002 agreeing probes before this pure rename; a final current-name run is required before push. The final required backlog after the generic leaf rename passes2695 entries with1002 agreeing probes. All existing test/probe bytes remain untouched; the new actual-chain probe retains SHA25616a33aeb0294e7ba6769914fbc94ed4c21b55132806e7b4e61a85eb577cf4713 and its27-case test retains SHA256391a97f09fbbb2f36e7cb42928a7b0f74d8e89d41ced324c05f64cb0dc7d1369.
